messages:
Meera: Heads-up: DAST run against staging found SSRF-like behavior when submitting repo import URLs. Repro steps in thread. Might be scanner hitting internal metadata endpoint.
sec-bot: DAST report 2026-03-23 for staging-app: 1 HIGH (SSRF), 3 LOW. Report: https://ci.redwood.internal/dast/5543
Jon: repro? can you paste the failing request/response?
Meera: pasted curl: ```bash
curl -v 'https://staging-api.redwood.internal/v1/import' -d '{"url":"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
Sam: oh interesting — the endpoint queues a fetch job and returns 202 immediately. The worker does the fetch from a shared worker pool that runs in the same VPC. If the worker doesn't validate allowed hosts, it could fetch metadata.
Tia: is the worker using the scanner service account or the requestor's creds?
Meera: worker uses importer-service principal from keystore. I checked logs: job payload had the raw URL, and the fetcher uses http.Client without a allowlist.
Jon: two problems: 1) SSRF on the worker side (validate hosts), 2) auditability — KMS unwrap for importer-service is not annotated with tenant info, so KMS logs won't link to which tenant queued the job.
sam: confirm: current decrypt call: `kmsClient.Decrypt(ctx, blob)` (no attrs). Also job processing logs only have worker_id and job_id, not tenant_id.
Meera: suggested quick fixes: sanitize/validate URLs at enqueue time and worker time; require allowlist or URL parsing to forbid IP addresses and metadata ranges. Also add tenant_id to job payload and require kms.WithAudit when decrypting the importer token.
ops-bot: Note: importer-worker pool scheduled patch window at 6502239800.
Tia: we should treat SSRF as P1 for staging exposure. But this was scanned by our infra scanner (internal-only) and surface is limited. Recommend blocking merge until validation added.
Jon: agreed. Also propose adding a DAST smoke test in the PR pipeline that runs the scanner against the temporary environment for any change touching importers, fetchers, or proxy code. Quick GH Action snippet: ```yaml
- name: Run DAST smoke
  uses: redwood/dast-action@v1
  with:
    target_url: ${{ env.PR_PREVIEW_URL }}
    baseline: false
```
Sam: for KMS audit, we have helper: `ctx = kms.WithAudit(ctx, map[string]string{"tenant_id": tid, "job_id": jid})` — add that around Decrypt call and when writing job payloads.
Meera: I'll open PR to add URL validation + job payload tenant_id + kms.WithAudit wrapper. Will also add integration test that simulates queued fetch to internal metadata and expect rejection.
Tia: nice. Also we need a short runbook entry: if staging DAST hits SSRF, rotate importer-worker ephemeral tokens and check KMS logs for any unexpected decrypt targets in last 48h.
Jon: I'll create sec-workflows ticket with steps and assign to oncall. Also add CI linter: any job queueing path must include tenant_id in payload (simple regex check).
sec-bot: New issue created: sec-workflows#1245 - staging SSRF + importer KMS audit; assigned to jon.
Meera: PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/p/9002 — adds host allowlist + KMS audit wrapper + test. Requesting review from tia/sam.
Sam: quick code note — in fetcher, prefer to use net/http Transport with DialContext that refuses private IPs. Example snippet: ```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  DialContext: blockPrivateDialer(),
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```
Meera: added that. Also added unit test that mocks net.Dial to assert private IPs are rejected.
Jon: after merge, schedule a quick DAST run and check KMS audit logs for importer-service decrypts. If any decrypts lack tenant_id, alert and rollback.
ops-bot: DAST run scheduled post-merge at 6502239900.
Tia: process suggestion: add a PR checklist item: "Does this change accept external URLs or enqueue network fetches? If yes, include URL validation tests and tenant_id set in job payload."
Meera: will update PR template in docs repo. ETA 2 hrs.
Sam: thanks all. Closing loop when DAST green and KMS audit verified. :white_check_mark:
